fields.m.setting: General education first grade with a push-in ESE teacher 60 min/day; 22 students
fields.m.beh: Vocal disruption: calling out, screaming, or repeating a word at a volume above the classroom level for at least 3 s, or banging the desk with both hands. Not: answering when called on, singing during music.
fields.m.reinf: Adult attention (teacher reprimand, redirection, or a para sitting beside her); strongest during independent seatwork when the teacher works with a small group.
fields.m.prec: Looks at the teacher, raises her hand briefly and drops it, taps the desk once.
fields.m.repdesc: Raises her hand but does not wait; no card or signal in use.
fields.m.pref: PA-1 (paired stimulus, 9/12): teacher helper jobs > stickers > reading with an adult > blocks.
fields.m.curr: Seatwork is at her level; she finishes early and waits with nothing to do.
fields.m.constraints: One teacher, no para during seatwork; a peer buddy system exists.
fields.m.safety: No injury; disrupts the small group daily.
fields.sel.why: From the model's questions; see the rationale on each card.
fields.cp[0].s0: Define the existing appropriate request (vocal, sign, gesture) that will produce the reinforcer.
fields.cp[0].s1: Reinforce every occurrence of the request under the EO with the functional reinforcer immediately.
fields.cp[0].s2: Withhold the reinforcer for problem behavior; if withholding is not feasible, arrange longer, higher-quality, and more immediate reinforcement for the request than problem behavior obtains (Athens & Vollmer, 2010).
fields.cp[0].s3: Watch for a temporary increase in problem behavior when a pre-existing response is reinforced (Derby et al., 1998, as reviewed by Tiger et al., 2008).
fields.cp[0].s4: Thin as for FCT once the request is reliable.
fields.cp[1].s0: Set the initial delivery interval below the mean baseline interresponse time (dense; near-continuous for severe behavior; Hagopian et al., 1994).
fields.cp[1].s1: Deliver the reinforcer (attention or the item) at each interval end regardless of behavior; keep the delivery brief and consistent.
fields.cp[1].s2: Withhold the reinforcer contingent on problem behavior (extinction) where feasible; delay a scheduled delivery briefly if problem behavior immediately precedes it.
fields.cp[1].s3: Thin the interval by steps when the criterion is met, toward a terminal schedule the setting can sustain.
fields.cp[1].s4: Introduce FCT after thinning rather than during a rich NCR schedule (Goh et al., 2000).
fields.cp[2].s0: Write a schedule of brief positive attention (e.g., 10 s of specific praise or conversation every 5 min) delivered by any adult in the room regardless of behavior.
fields.cp[2].s1: Set the interval below the baseline mean interresponse time at first; use a timer or app so delivery does not depend on the behavior.
fields.cp[2].s2: If the behavior occurs just before a scheduled delivery, delay it briefly.
fields.cp[2].s3: Thin the schedule as the behavior stays low; do not run a rich schedule at the same time as FCT acquisition (Goh, Iwata, & DeLeon, 2000).
fields.cp[3].s0: Before the routine in which the behavior occurs, provide free access to the maintaining reinforcer (attention or the item) for a set period.
fields.cp[3].s1: Begin the routine immediately after; expect lower value of the reinforcer and less behavior for a limited window.
fields.cp[3].s2: Record the length of the effect and adjust timing; combine with the consequence components rather than relying on it alone.
fields.cp[4].s0: Identify from the SP-1 and ABC-1 data which peers, locations, and materials precede the behavior.
fields.cp[4].s1: Seat the student away from evocative peers and doorways (or near the exit route when elopement is the target and a staff member sits between), with materials within reach and the break area visible.
fields.cp[4].s2: Use row seating for independent work; rearrange only after data show a problem with the current arrangement.
fields.cp[4].s3: Review the arrangement at each plan review.
fields.cp[5].s0: At arrival, check the setting events the assessment identified (sleep, illness, allergy symptoms, missed medication, conflict on the bus or at home, hunger) with the parent note or a brief check.
fields.cp[5].s1: When a setting event is present, run the neutralizing routine: a preferred activity first, reduced or shortened demands, extra noncontingent attention, and choice for that morning (Horner et al., 1997).
fields.cp[5].s2: Record the setting event and the routine used on the data sheet; report medical setting events to the nurse.
fields.cp[6].s0: Identify the specific social consequence the student prefers (form of praise, tickles, conversation, high five) with a social-interaction preference assessment (Smaby et al., 2007; Call et al., 2013).
fields.cp[6].s1: Deliver it immediately and enthusiastically for the target response; keep it brief.
fields.cp[6].s2: Test it under intermittent schedules before relying on it; if it weakens, back it with tangibles or tokens.
fields.cp[7].s0: Completing a unit schedule (e.g., FR 3 correct) earns a token; completing the exchange schedule (e.g., 5 tokens) earns the backup reinforcer.
fields.cp[7].s1: Establish tokens by pairing with immediate exchange at first (exchange after 1 token), then lengthen the exchange requirement.
fields.cp[7].s2: Offer a menu of backup reinforcers to limit satiation; keep the exchange schedule dense enough to contact the backup daily.
fields.cp[7].s3: Thin the unit schedule before the exchange schedule.
fields.cp[8].s0: Line up 5–7 items; the student approaches one and receives brief access; remove it and re-present the rest until all are chosen or 30 s passes without a choice.
fields.cp[8].s1: Repeat 3–5 times; rank by mean selection order or percentage.
fields.cp[8].s2: Use the brief version before sessions to track daily shifts (DeLeon et al., 2001).
fields.cp[9].s0: Present every pair of items once (left–right counterbalanced); record the item approached; deliver brief access to it.
fields.cp[9].s1: Rank items by percentage of trials selected; high preference ≥ 80%.
fields.cp[9].s2: Assess edible and leisure classes separately; caregiver nominations (RAISD; Fisher et al., 1996) build the array.
fields.cp[10].s0: Reinforce every occurrence of the target response during acquisition.
fields.cp[10].s1: Hold CRF until the response is independent and stable.
fields.cp[10].s2: Thin only by a planned schedule (see the thinning ladder).
fields.cp[11].s0: Begin with the prompt that guarantees the response (e.g., full physical), delivered immediately with the instruction.
fields.cp[11].s1: Reduce to the next less intrusive level after the criterion (e.g., 3 consecutive correct); return one level after 2 errors.
fields.cp[11].s2: Reinforce prompted responses during acquisition; differentially reinforce unprompted responses once they appear.
fields.cp[11].s3: Use when errors evoke problem behavior or the response is new.
fields.cp[12].s0: Begin with a 0-s delay between instruction and prompt; increase the delay in small steps (e.g., 1 s per session or per criterion) as unprompted responses appear.
fields.cp[12].s1: Transfer of control is shown when the learner responds before the prompt; keep the terminal delay short enough to prevent errors.
fields.cp[12].s2: Reinforce unprompted responses more richly than prompted ones.
fields.cp[13].s0: Compare candidate prompt types (vocal, model, physical) or hierarchies (MTL vs LTM) on equivalent skill sets in an alternating-treatments design.
fields.cp[13].s1: Select the procedure that produced the fastest acquisition with the fewest errors and least problem behavior.
fields.cp[13].s2: Re-run when a new response class is introduced.
fields.cp[14].s0: After an error, model or deliver the correct response, then re-present the instruction and require an independent (or least-prompted) correct response before moving on.
fields.cp[14].s1: Reinforce the corrected response with praise only; reserve the token or item for unprompted responses.
fields.cp[15].s0: Begin with the FCR honored immediately; introduce a signaled delay of a few seconds, then lengthen it stepwise (e.g., 5 → 15 → 30 → 60 s → several minutes) as problem behavior stays low.
fields.cp[15].s1: During the delay, prompt and reinforce engagement in an alternative activity or work (the delay is filled, not empty).
fields.cp[15].s2: Add unpredictable denials with the tolerance response once delays are tolerated.
fields.cp[15].s3: Step back one level after two sessions with problem behavior during the delay.
fields.cp[16].s0: Select the mand: recognizable to novel listeners, quickly acquired, less effortful than the problem behavior; a card or switch may precede a vocal form (Tiger et al., 2008).
fields.cp[16].s1: Start in a controlled setting with a trained implementer; contrive the establishing operation (present the demand / divert attention / remove the item) several times per session.
fields.cp[16].s2: Prompt the mand at the EO: most-to-least (physical prompt immediately, faded across trials; Fisher et al., 1993) or least-to-most with a 5-s progressive delay (Shirley et al., 1997).
fields.cp[16].s3: Reinforce every mand with the functional reinforcer immediately (CRF); a break of 1 min, 20–30 s of attention, or the item.
fields.cp[16].s4: Withhold the reinforcer for the problem behavior (extinction); if problem behavior occurs with the mand, do not reinforce and re-present the EO (Harding et al., 2009).
fields.cp[16].s5: For escape: chain a work requirement before the mand opportunity and raise it as behavior improves (Lalli et al., 1995; Harding et al., 2009).
fields.cp[16].s6: Thin with a signaled multiple schedule (reinforcement and extinction periods with distinct cues; Hanley et al., 2001) or a signaled delay faded from 1 s toward 30 s (Fisher et al., 2000); provide alternative reinforcers during extinction periods (Hagopian et al., 2011).
fields.cp[16].s7: Add trainers and settings, include common stimuli, and probe untrained contexts; increase response complexity after acquisition.
fields.cp[17].s0: After the tolerance response, present one contextually appropriate behavior (relinquish the item, transition, or complete one instruction) before the synthesized reinforcers are delivered.
fields.cp[17].s1: Lengthen the chain and vary its content unpredictably (one instruction → three → a short task → a full routine) while keeping some trials in which the FCR is honored immediately.
fields.cp[17].s2: Reinforce the chain with the synthesized reinforcers at a decreasing but unpredictable probability; add praise throughout.
fields.cp[17].s3: Extend to new implementers and settings with the same sequence; probe the natural routine before and after.
fields.cp[18].s0: Identify the reinforcer and the establishing operation that makes it valuable (deprivation, an interrupted chain, a missing item).
fields.cp[18].s1: Contrive the EO (interrupt a chain by withholding a needed item; present the preferred item and remove it) and wait briefly for the mand.
fields.cp[18].s2: Prompt the mand form (vocal, sign, picture, device) and deliver the specific reinforcer immediately; fade prompts with a progressive delay so the EO, not the prompt, controls the mand (Sweeney-Kerwin et al., 2007).
fields.cp[18].s3: Run many trials per session across items; record prompted and unprompted mands.
fields.cp[19].s0: Capture naturally occurring EOs during routines (snack, play, transitions); pause and wait for the mand before providing the item or action.
fields.cp[19].s1: Prompt only as needed, fade quickly, and reinforce with the item requested.
fields.cp[19].s2: Rotate across settings, listeners, and items to build generalized manding; record mands per hour in the natural routine.
fields.cp[20].s0: Before the activity, have the student state what they will do ("I will use the break card if the work is hard"); reinforce the statement at first (reinforce-saying phase).
fields.cp[20].s1: Shift reinforcement to correspondence: reinforce only when the stated behavior occurs (reinforce-correspondence phase); use say-then-do ordering (Israel & O'Leary, 1973).
fields.cp[20].s2: Fade to intermittent checks and to the student's own review of correspondence.
fields.cp[20].s3: Use when the student can state a plan and the goal is self-management across settings.
fields.cp[21].s0: Score the Milestones (mand, tact, listener, VP-MTS, play, social, imitation, echoic, intraverbal, group, linguistic, reading, writing, math) and the Barriers assessment.
fields.cp[21].s1: Select replacement and skill targets at the student's current level; treat barriers (e.g., defective mands, prompt dependence, behavior problems) as programming priorities.
fields.cp[21].s2: Re-score at the plan review interval; use the Transition assessment for placement decisions.
fields.cp[22].s0: Assess the must-have skills first: requesting, waiting after requests, accepting removals and transitions, completing brief tasks, accepting "no," and health and safety routines.
fields.cp[22].s1: Select the alternative method of speaking (vocal, sign, picture, device) from the student's repertoire and teach requests first.
fields.cp[22].s2: Sequence the remaining must-have skills alongside the reduction plan; record the level of prompting and the settings in which each skill occurs.
fields.cp[23].p2: Not needed (no injury); if screaming lasts 3 minutes, the resource teacher takes the small group to the hall and the class continues.
fields.cp[23].s0: On the precursor: At the brief hand-raise or desk tap: come within 1 m, say "I see your hand", and deliver 15 s of attention if the hand stays up (prompt the card).
fields.cp[23].s1: On the target behavior: Keep attention on the small group; do not look at or speak to her; the peer buddy continues; at the first 5 s of quiet, deliver attention per the schedule (no extinction of attention from peers is attempted).
fields.cp[23].s2: After the episode: Return to the schedule of attention at the next interval; record the episode on DD-1.
fields.cp[23].s3: Staff do not: Do not reprimand, redirect verbally, or send a para to sit with her during the outburst; do not move her seat during the episode.
fields.cp[23].s4: Record the episode, the step used, and whether the reinforcer was contacted (integrity error).
fields.cp[23].s5: Crisis procedure applies only when the safety trigger is met and is documented separately.
fields.cp[24].bsrc: Fixed-time attention every minute, cued by a vibrating timer, for attention-maintained disruption during group lessons (Noel & Getch, 2016)
fields.cp[24].p0: FT 1 min, set from the baseline rate of adult attention (praise or reprimands) rounded to the nearest minute
fields.cp[24].p1: one brief neutral comment addressed to the student within 5 s of the cue
fields.cp[24].s0: During baseline, count how often adults attend to the student (praise or reprimands) and use that rate to set the fixed-time interval (1 min here).
fields.cp[24].s1: Train staff in about 1 h with a rationale, a 10-min video model, and 10 min of practice until they deliver 80% of comments on time.
fields.cp[24].s2: Set a vibrating timer to buzz every minute during the target activity (a 10-min social-skills lesson).
fields.cp[24].s3: At each buzz, give the student a short neutral comment by name within 5 s.
fields.cp[24].s4: Keep comments neutral: no praise, no reprimand, and not addressed to the whole group.
fields.cp[24].s5: Continue regular instruction with the rest of the group between cues.
fields.cp[24].data: frequency of negative talk and property destruction per session (event recording), and percentage of cues followed by an on-time comment (staff fidelity)
fields.cp[24].mat: vibrating interval timer, list of sample neutral comments
fields.cp[25].bsrc: Functional communication training with extinction and gradual, signaled schedule thinning (practice guide) (Tiger et al., 2008)
fields.cp[25].p0: a low-effort response that unfamiliar people will recognize and the student can learn fast, such as a picture exchange, a single sign, a voice-output button or a short vocal request; an existing response such as signing 'all done' can be strengthened; make it more complex once problem behavior is low
fields.cp[25].p1: most-to-least (physical prompt as soon as the motivating situation is set up, then faded in intensity) or least-to-most with a delay (wait about 5 s, then a vocal or physical prompt, with the delay lengthened over trials)
fields.cp[25].p2: the reinforcer found in the functional analysis, given every time at first; if extinction cannot be used, make reinforcement for the communication longer, better, faster or more frequent than for problem behavior
fields.cp[25].p3: withhold the maintaining reinforcer after problem behavior from the start of treatment
fields.cp[25].p4: lengthen a delay to reinforcement starting at 1 s with a signal that it is coming; or alternate signaled periods when requests are and are not honored (for example two colored cards); for escape, raise the amount of work required before a break request is honored
fields.cp[25].p5: a schedule caregivers can keep up; the guide cites success with requests honored only during signaled periods covering about 20% of the time
fields.cp[25].s0: Confirm the maintaining reinforcer with a functional analysis before starting.
fields.cp[25].s1: Pick a communication response that is low effort, easy for unfamiliar people to recognize, and quick to learn.
fields.cp[25].s2: Begin with a trained interventionist in a safe, controlled setting and create many practice opportunities by setting up the motivating situation (remove the item, withhold attention, or present the task).
fields.cp[25].s3: Prompt the communication response either right away (most-to-least) or after a short wait such as 5 s (least-to-most with a delay), and fade the prompt over trials.
fields.cp[25].s4: Deliver the maintaining reinforcer every time the student communicates during initial training.
fields.cp[25].s5: Withhold the maintaining reinforcer after problem behavior.
fields.cp[25].s6: Once problem behavior is low, thin reinforcement gradually using a signaled delay starting at 1 s, signaled periods when requests can and cannot be honored, or, for escape, more work before the break request is honored.
fields.cp[25].s7: Offer other preferred items during delays or unavailable periods to compete with problem behavior during thinning.
fields.cp[25].s8: Extend training across several trainers and settings, bring in materials from the classroom, train in each needed setting, and teach caregivers how to respond.
fields.cp[25].s9: Increase the complexity of the communication response over time, for example a full request such as 'May I have ___, please'.
fields.cp[25].data: Rate of problem behavior and of independent communication responses per session, prompt level used, and the current thinning step, plus probes in each setting and with each caregiver, recorded on Form DD-1.
fields.cp[25].mat: Communication materials (picture cards, voice-output device or sign), the reinforcer identified in the functional analysis, signals for reinforcement availability such as colored cards, a timer, and a protected setting for early training.
fields.sch.1: no, time is easier to track
fields.ec.0: no, the prompting procedure is errorless
fields.sk.chosen: DT_PROG, FCT, SBT_CAB, MAND_CONT, MAND_NET, SAYDO, VBMAPP, EFL
fields.rb.prec: At the brief hand-raise or desk tap: come within 1 m, say "I see your hand", and deliver 15 s of attention if the hand stays up (prompt the card).
fields.rb.target: Keep attention on the small group; do not look at or speak to her; the peer buddy continues; at the first 5 s of quiet, deliver attention per the schedule (no extinction of attention from peers is attempted).
fields.rb.after: Return to the schedule of attention at the next interval; record the episode on DD-1.
fields.rb.not: Do not reprimand, redirect verbally, or send a para to sit with her during the outburst; do not move her seat during the episode.
fields.rb.crisis: Not needed (no injury); if screaming lasts 3 minutes, the resource teacher takes the small group to the hall and the class continues.
fields.p.visit: Weekly 30-minute visit: observe one session, score the integrity checklist, give feedback, model any step under 80%.
fields.p.pre: Probes before the plan starts: the target and the replacement behavior in 3 settings (class, specials, cafeteria) with 2 adults.
fields.p.gen: Train with two adults and in two settings from the first week; the natural cue (the demand itself) is the SD; the card goes with the student.
fields.p.post: Probes in the untrained setting at 2 and 4 weeks after criterion; monthly after.
fields.p.complex: The simple response first; the longer form once the simple one is at criterion.
fields.p.design: Baseline to treatment with the EA-1 treatment sheet; reversal only if the team agrees.
